full_judgment:
2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are that the petitioner (the plaintiff) filed Other Suit No. 150 of 1985 in the first Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Chittagong. The suit was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong and renumbered as Other Suit No. 50 of 1992 against the defendant respondents. The suit has been filed for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and also for khas possession if the plaintiff is found to be out of possession of the suit land during pendency of the suit. The plaintiff has also prayed for further declaration that the deed of sale dated 14.11.1961 and the bainanamas dated 04.03.1985, 13.03.1985, 14.03.1985, 16.03.1985 and 17.03.1985 are forged, illegal, fraudulent, collusive and also for permanent injunction. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Jaha Box and the A.S. record was prepared in his name in Khatian Nos. 43 and 45. While in possession, he transferred the suit land to Nazrul Islam Chowdhury by a deed of sale dated 12.05.1936, which thereafter transferred the suit land to Mohammad Mia Chowdhury by a deed of sale dated 23.07.1958 and his name was recorded in P.S. and B.S. khatians. He constructed boundary wall and used to cultivate various seasonal crops and planted different kinds of trees there. On 14.02.1985, Mohammad Mia Chowdhury transferred the suit land to the plaintiff by a registered deed of exchange and the plaintiff was inducted into possession thereof. The plaintiff got the jams separated and mutated his name in Mutation Case No. 884 of 1984-1985. After that, defendant No. 1 filed an application for vacating the earlier order of mutation in favour of the plaintiff. Defendant No. 1 claimed that he got the suit land from proforma defendant No. 13, Mohammad Mia Chowdhury, on the basis of a registered deed of sale dated 14.11.1961. The plaintiff contacted proforma-defendant No. 13 who denied executing such deed of sale in favour off defendant No.  1. After obtaining certified copy of the deed of sale standing in the name of defendant No. 1, the plaintiff lodged a complaint with the Anti-Corruption Department for taking appropriate action against the persons involved in creating the forged deed. After that, defendant No. 1 disclosed in Settlement Objection Case No. 881 of 1983 that he got his name recorded in B.S. record and that proforma defendant No. 13 executed a power of attorney on 04.12.1984 in favour of defendant Nos. 2-4 authorising them to for manage and to sell the disputed land. He further disclosed that proforma defendant No. 13 executed various bainanamas in favour of defendant Nos. 6-12. After that, the plaintiff was served with a notice in respect of CID entry No.  1045 dated 24.03.1985 issued from the Double mooring Police Station. The Assistant Commissioner along with the Officer-in-Charge of Chittagong Metropolitan Police (C.M.P) held a local inquiry on 13.04.1985 at Rawzan Health Complex where proforma defendant No. 13 was undergoing treatment and defendant No. 13 categorically denied executing and registering the disputed deed of sale in favour of defendant No. 1. After that, defendant No. 1 and his son with other accomplices being armed with deadly weapons ransacked the darwan's shed of the plaintiff on the suit land and removed the signboard and assaulted the darwan who ran away in fear for his life. Hence, the plaintiff filed the instant suit. 

 3. Respondent No. 1 (defendant No. 1) contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material Statements made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that the suit is not maintainable in the eye of law and is barred by section 39 of the Specific Relief Act and that the suit is also barred by the principles of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence. The plaintiff has not acquired any right, title and interest in the schedule property by his alleged deed of exchange dated 14.12.1985 and the plaintiff is not in possession of the suit property or any part thereof. As such, the plaintiff is not entitled to get the relief as sought without a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khan possession. Mohammad Miah Chowdhury, proforma defendant No. 13, was the owner of the suit land by purchase but it was not correct that B.S. khatian was recorded in his name or he constructed any boundary wall or produced any seasonal crops or planted any tree there. It is further stated that the suit land originally belonged to Jaha Box, who transferred the suit land to Md. Nurul Islam Chowdhury on 12.05.1936, who again transferred it to pro-forma defendant No. 13 Mohammad Miah Chowdhury on 23.07.1958. On 14.11.1961, Mohammad Miah Chowdhury again transferred the suit land to defendant No.  1 and handed over possession thereof to him. Defendant No. 1 has been possessing the suit land by producing various types of vegetables including planting trees and a resort, namely, "Tawua Kabab" house was there. During the last survey, the suit land was correctly recorded in the B.S. khatian and defendant No. 1 has been paying rents and taxes since its purchase. After purchase of the suit land by defendant No. 1 in 1961, the P.S. record was wrongly recorded in the name of proforma defendant No. 13. Taking this advantage the plaintiff created a deed of exchange with proforma defendant No, 13 on 14.02.1985. By creating the forged deed, the plaintiff having no possession in the suit land filed the suit. The plaintiff lodged a complaint with the Bureau of Anti-Corruption against the deed of sale executed and registered in 1961 by proforma defendant No. 13. The Police Commissioner obtained thumb impression of Mohammad Mia Chowdhury to compare the same with that appearing in the deed of sale dated 14.11.1961 by the finger print expert. The finger print expert opined that the thumb impression appearing in the deed of sale dated 14.11.1961 was that of Mohammad Mia Chowdhury. As such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
